A1.justification: Both complete, readable PDFs describe the same ORES/RAS research. Main text, figures, tables and Appendices A-F can be matched despite the changed title and figure renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original RAS evaluations on ORES, RES and GRES, with quantitative results, ablations and additional appendix experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds qualitative comparisons on underwater and cartoon images in Appendix F.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1-3.2 and Appendix A retain the same mask tokenization, visual encoder ensemble, non-autoregressive binary selection, training stages and objectives. The new generalization discussion introduces no method modification.

E1.justification: New Figure C evaluates underwater fish and cartoon cloud segmentation, adding two qualitative test scenarios. Existing training and benchmark datasets remain unchanged; the clarification about EntitySeg image sources does not establish changed dataset composition.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding benchmark tables and existing appendix experiments. The new OOD examples reuse GSVA13B, which was already evaluated against RAS.

E3.justification: Existing splits, preprocessing, metrics, training budgets, model configurations and ablation procedures are unchanged. The new OOD images extend qualitative evaluation without introducing a documented change in evaluation procedure.

E4.justification: Appendix F adds a qualitative generalization check comparing RAS and GSVA on two OOD examples. Existing candidate-quality analyses, ablations, baseline finetuning and prompt-conversion experiments are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed-based variability, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new qualitative comparison adds no uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: New Figure C shows better fish and cloud segmentation by RAS13B with SAM than GSVA13B on the displayed examples. Numerical results in Tables 3-8 and A-D, and the existing qualitative results, are unchanged.

T1.justification: No mathematical definitions, derivations, assumptions or proofs are added or revised. The task formulation and optimization reasoning remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same claims about ORES, RAS, the two datasets and benchmark performance. The more specific title does not redefine the scientific contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix F newly interprets the OOD examples as evidence of strong generalization and attributes this to separating mask generation from selection and benefiting from SAM. This mechanism attribution is not supported by a new controlled ablation.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 clarifies that the existing EntitySeg-derived images come from multiple sources beyond MS-COCO. New acknowledgments disclose computing facilities and services; Appendix A's implementation recipe and project access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix F adds a limited positioning statement contrasting RAS's generalization beyond MS-COCO with prior work's benchmark focus. The related-work section and cited-work set remain unchanged; reference author and venue updates are bibliographic only.

P1.justification: v2 changes the title, adds equal-advising information, acknowledgments and an appendix heading, and makes localized prose clarifications. The section organization and most wording remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds OOD Figure C and renumbers the existing qualitative Figure C as D. It also revises figure headers, highlights table rows and rearranges appendix tables and text, while preserving existing image panels and table contents.

improvement.justification: The new OOD comparisons make behavior outside the previously illustrated scenarios inspectable, while clearer dataset provenance and figure labeling improve transparency. Existing experimental evidence is preserved. The gain is limited: two qualitative examples do not establish broad OOD robustness or isolate the claimed role of SAM.
